title: MedTech POC hosting synthesis and proposed hybrid topology
content:
Context:
This is the working synthesis from the 2025-08-06 workshop with AcuWave (medical-device + clinician workflow POC). Goal: give product and infra owners a single-page decision guide that maps the customer constraints to a recommended hosting topology (hosted / dedicated / private / hybrid), a short rollout plan, and the biggest open questions that need engineering follow-up. This doc is intentionally terse — think cheat-sheet + annotated notes rather than a polished PRD.

Customer constraints and non-functional priorities (summary):
- Data sensitivity: high. Clinical note text will be pseudo-anonymized in early POC but long term needs PHI-safe handling and audit logs.
- Latency: interactive clinician flows require sub-400ms median response for short queries (<=256 tokens) in target region.
- Throughput: steady 40 qps during clinic hours, bursty spikes to 120 qps for batch review windows.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-tier — willing to pay for predictability (reserved capacity) but wants to avoid large upfront on-prem procurement during POC.
- Connectivity: hospitals sometimes have segmented networks and strict egress policies; some pilot sites will be air-gapped or limited egress.
- Compliance: eventual SOC2 + HIPAA expectations; POC should not block these conversations.

POC scenarios we considered:
A) Single-hosted: Redwood hosted API in us-east with VPC peering and dedicated tenant config for logs. Good for fastest time-to-value.
B) Dedicated-reserved: Dedicated Redwood cluster in a cloud VPC (customer-controlled VPC peering), predictable latency/cost, customer keys in KMS.
C) Private-edge: Private deployment in hospital subnet (on-prem or VPC-only), limited egress, full control for PHI.
D) Hybrid-fallback: Private-edge for clinical requests, hosted for non-sensitive analytics and fallback; routing based on tag or header.

Recommendation (short):
Start POC with a Hybrid-fallback topology (D) implemented as a staged path: hosted prototype -> dedicated-reserved for pilot -> optional private-edge for regulated sites. Reasoning: minimizes time-to-value while producing artifacts (audit logs, KMS integration, routing rules) required for moving to dedicated/private. Also supports air-gapped pilot sites later with minimal re-architecture if we keep API surface stable.

Mapping of constraints to solution levers: (how the hybrid topology maps to customer needs)
- Data sensitivity: Private-edge covers highest risk sites. For hosted/dedicated portions, enforce encrypted-at-rest, customer-managed keys (KMS), token-level audit logs and redact/pseudonymization pipeline.
- Latency: Keep small GPU-backed dedicated pool for latency-sensitive lanes (256-token path) with hot KV-cache; hosted fallback uses slightly larger model variant to preserve cost during non-critical loads.
- Throughput: Autoscaled dedicated pool with burst capacity to hosted if utilization threshold crossed (circuit-breaker policy).
- Connectivity: Use a lightweight connector (reverse VPN / TLS tunnel) that can be deployed to hospital DMZ to enable private-edge control-plane heartbeat without full upstream egress.

Architecture sketch (operational notes):
1) API contract: Keep identical endpoint semantics across all venues. Add header x-rdwood-routing-preference: private|dedicated|hosted to let customer explicit route for testing.
2) Routing & policy engine: Route by tenant config -> primary venue (private if available) -> secondary (dedicated) -> fallthrough (hosted). Implement health checks and KV-cache sync policy (TTL-based eventual consistency).
3) Model variants: Provide two model families for the POC: "fast-256" (optimized latency quantized variant) and "balanced-1k" (better quality, higher latency). Ship with automatic fallback mapping for long-context requests.
4) Security & compliance: Use HSM/KMS for private keys, keep audit logs central but access-restricted; for private-edge deploy light-weight log forwarder that mirrors anonymized metrics to console and keeps raw PHI locally.
5) Observability: Instrument token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, per-model error counts. Add alerting for drift in hallucination rate measured by sentinel prompt set (see linked artifact CONFLUENCE-3892).

Rollout plan for the POC (6-week runway):
Week 0-1: Kickoff + environment provisioning (hosted sandbox + dedicated reserved instance request).
Week 2: Basic hosted prototype integrated into clinician UI (feature flags). Preliminary latency SLA verification.
Week 3: Provision dedicated pool, wire KMS integration + tenant-level audit logs. Run smoke tests.
Week 4: Deploy hybrid router and set default routing to dedicated. Begin collecting A/B metrics (hosted vs dedicated).
Week 5: Pilot private-edge at 1 hospital (privacy review + connector deployment). Validate egress constraints and log redaction.
Week 6: Consolidate findings, cost model, recommended path (go/no-go to enter extended pilot).

Open technical risks & follow-ups (who/owner):
- Connector stability for segmented networks (SRE / infra - Omar) — test matrix for intermittent connectivity, reconnect semantics, and local cache eviction.
- Audit log volume and retention cost (FinOps + Observability - Marco) — estimate compressed storage delta for token-level audit logs; consider sampling strategy for high-volume clinics.
- Model quality regressions across quantized variants (Applied ML - Tanya) — run eval harness on clinical prompts and surface failure modes.
- Encryption boundary in hybrid mode (Security - Leah) — define exactly which artifacts travel to hosted fallback and encrypt in transit + at rest.

Quick cost heuristics (back-of-envelope):
- Hosted-only initial prototype: low infra cost (~$700-$1.5k/week depending on test scale) but variable per-token charges.
- Dedicated reserved (small pool for 40 qps): predictable ~$20k/month effective commit for GPU capacity (example for M60-like quota).
- Private-edge: high one-time integration + per-site ops (~$8k-$25k per site setup + runbooks, depending on on-prem hardware).
These numbers intentionally broad — follow-up required with FinOps for exact quote.

Acceptance / exit criteria for POC:
- Median latency <=420ms on dedicated path for 256-token queries in clinic region (measured over 3 consecutive days).
- Evidence of safe PHI handling: audit trails present + successful local log redaction test at pilot site.
- Cost model for 3 scaling scenarios (10, 50, 200 clinics) with committed vs on-demand numbers.
- ML quality gate: sentinel prompt set pass rate delta <5% when moving from balanced to fast variant.

Appendix: quick checklist for next engineering spike
- Define IP allowlist + TLS cert stitching approach for connector. (Action: Omar)
- Draft KMS key rotation and per-tenant access policy doc (Action: Security)
- Add sampling spec for audit logs (Action: Observability)
- Create test harness to compare fast-256 vs balanced-1k on clinical prompt set (Action: Tanya)
- Add canary rollout config to Console for routing toggles and rollback (Action: Console team)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Customer seemed comfortable with a hybrid path because it aligns with their procurement timeline (no heavy upfront hardware for POC).
- Keep experiment small: prove routing, KMS + audit first — model quality improvements are parallel but not blocking.
- If private-edge proves brittle, consider "on-prem API gateway" pattern where compute remains in Redwood Dedicated but gateway/local proxy holds PHI and does pre/post-processing.

Timestamped edits: 2025-08-12 initial draft by Leah; 2025-08-14 added rollout timeline and cost heuristics (Marco); 2025-08-20 replaced tentative numbers after quick FinOps sync (Marco).
